_comment: Scan self-checks for the NAILS forensic oracle in REAL-image mode (ORACLE_IMAGES_DIR). run-scan.sh selects this file instead of controls.json when scanning the before/control/after.raw the e2e disk-forensics harness retained (nix/e2e-tests/tests/forensic/13-oracle-images.nix). The three positive controls are @oracle.example addresses that run-scan.sh injects, in place, into the baseline carrier files on a THROWAWAY working copy of after.raw only (before.raw, control.raw and the retained after.raw are never modified); the carrier files themselves (/var/log/wtmp.db, /var/lib/lastlog/lastlog2.db, /var/log/pacman.log) were planted address-free on the decoy before the baseline snapshot, so they are present on all three images and only the injected address is new. bulk_extractor carves each address from the raw image bytes with no format-aware parser, so each surfaces at the exact (bulk_extractor, email, <address>) key pinned below -- the same addresses the synthetic controls.json uses, so the pins are reusable. The canary is the reserved address the e2e spec plants at /var/lib/nails-oracle/canary on every image; bulk_extractor carves it the same way, so its scan key is (bulk_extractor, email, canary@oracle.example). Because the canary is fixed at e2e time, run-scan.sh does NOT rotate it in this mode. Keep these in step with what forensic/13 plants and what run-scan.sh injects.

positive_controls.name: wtmpdb-boot
positive_controls.note: Injected as the remote-host text column of a wtmpdb login row appended to /var/log/wtmp.db on the after working copy.

positive_controls.name: lastlog2
positive_controls.note: Injected as the remote-host text column of a lastlog2 row appended to /var/lib/lastlog/lastlog2.db on the after working copy.

positive_controls.name: pkg-history
positive_controls.note: Injected as a comment in a pacman history line appended to /var/log/pacman.log on the after working copy.
